title: Provisioning request lifecycle, SLA commitments, and autoscale rule templates
creator: Marina Patel
description: Define and deliver an end-to-end provisioning request lifecycle for Dedicated capacity that ties requested throughput guarantees to a standard approval flow, autoscaling policy templates, and fleet control knobs. The goal is to make capacity requests predictable for customers and ops, reduce manual back-and-forth during approvals, and ensure autoscaling behavior (bursting, scale floor/ceiling, buffer) is encoded into the reservation so SLAs can be met.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can submit a provisioning request via Console or API with fields: requested RPS/throughput, peak window, expected qps distribution, preferred region, duration, and SLAs
Backend stores a normalized capacity profile and associates one of 3 autoscaling policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive)
Approvers see a pre-populated justification card with cost estimate, expected contention risk, and suggested reservation size
Approval action triggers creation of a Dedicated reservation object and sends a provisioning job to infra with capacity buffer applied
Console shows provisioning status, expected go-live ETA, and updateable autoscale parameters post-provisioning
Audit log entries are created for request, approval, provisioning start/complete, and all parameter changes
tasks: Write PRD: request schema, autoscale templates, approval rules, and audit requirements (owner: PM)
Design Console UX for request form and approver review card (owner: Design)
Backend normalization: capacity profile calculator + cost estimator (owner: ENG)
Implement autoscale templates and policy enforcement in scheduler (owner: ENG)
Integrate KMS/audit logging for approval events (owner: Security)
E2E tests for request -> approve -> provision -> cancel (owner: QA)
Run canary with 3 pilot customers and capture telemetry (owner: Solutions)
Prepare runbook for SRE for failed provisioning or partial capacity fulfillment (owner: SRE)
comments: 2026-02-22 Marina Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Key constraint: we must support both console and API request flows to avoid sales-only bottlenecks.
2026-02-28 Diego Morales: Proposal to use three autoscale templates to balance complexity vs. flexibility — conservative, balanced, aggressive. Need ENG input on safe defaults for buffer percentages.
2026-03-04 Priya Rao (Design): Initial mockups for the request form uploaded to Drive. Link included.
2026-03-07 Anika Singh (Sales Eng): Pilot customers want a simple toggle for 'guaranteed throughput' vs 'best-effort' — recommends including a checkbox that maps to policy selection.
2026-03-10 Diego Morales: Security flagged audit retention requirement (7 years for enterprise customers). Added to scope; security review required.
success_metrics: Time from request submission to approval < 72 hours for standard requests
Number of manual approval clarifications per request < 0.25 avg
Pilot customers report SLA confidence >= 4/5 in feedback survey
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): Console + API form, autoscale templates, non-production provisioning (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot): Offer to 3 pilot customers with dedicated CSM and runbook support (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (general availability): Open to all accounts with quota guardrails and default conservative template (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (post-GA): Add UI for custom autoscale tweaks and retrospective cost reconciliation (ongoing)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: three templates reduces decision fatigue but limits custom tuning; plan to expose advanced knobs post-GA
Risk: inaccurate customer-provided traffic profiles could lead to under-provisioning — mitigated by default buffer and a mandatory peak-window field
Operational cost vs SLA: we will recommend a conservative buffer for new reservations and allow higher guaranteed rates via manual review to control spend
Security: approval actions must be auditable and integrate with SSO roles — increases implementation complexity
